headline: Read the original low bit and append it to a growing reversed result
statement: Reverse the order of all 32 bits of an unsigned 32-bit integer n and return the resulting unsigned integer. Leading zero bits participate in the reversal.
intuition: Read the input from its least significant bit. Shift the result left to make room, then append that input bit. Repeat for all 32 positions, including zeros. Reading bits in this order writes their original positions in reverse order.
approach: Repeat 32 times: shift result left and append n&1.
Shift n right to expose the next input bit.
correctness: After k iterations, result consists of the original lowest k bits in reverse order, by shifting the existing sequence and appending the next low bit. Exactly 32 iterations include every position, so the final sequence is the full bit reversal.
bruteForce: Format a padded 32-character binary string, reverse it, and parse it back; correct but allocates a string.

complexity.explanation: Exactly 32 iterations each perform one mask, two shifts, and one bit append. The fixed width and two scalar integers make both time and additional storage constant.

pitfalls: Stopping when n becomes zero omits leading zero positions.
Python integers are unbounded, so the fixed loop supplies the 32-bit width.
